entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 13 Ro 13:1-14 . Same Subject Continued--Political and Social Relations--Motives. 1-2. Let every soul-- every man of you be subject unto the higher powers-- or, "submit himself to the authorities that are above him." For there is no power-- "no authority" but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God-- "have been ordained of God."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16646"/><div sID="gen32606" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16646"/><hi type="bold">5. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath--</hi>for fear of the magistrate's vengeance.<div eID="gen32606" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32607" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">but also for conscience' sake--</hi>from reverence for God's authority. It is of Magistracy in general, considered as a divine ordinance, that this is spoken: and the statement applies equally to all forms of government, from an unchecked despotism--such as flourished when this was written, under the Emperor Nero--to a pure democracy. The inalienable right of all subjects to endeavor to alter or improve the form of government under which they live is left untouched here. But since Christians were constantly charged with turning the world upside down, and since there certainly were elements enough in Christianity of moral and social revolution to give plausibility to the charge, and tempt noble spirits, crushed under misgovernment, to take redress into their own hands, it was of special importance that the pacific, submissive, loyal spirit of those Christians who resided at the great seat of political power, should furnish a visible refutation of this charge. <div eID="gen32607" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 12. The night-- of evil is far spent, the day-- of consummated triumph over it is at hand: let us therefore cast off-- as a dress the works of darkness-- all works holding of the kingdom and period of darkness, with which, as followers of the risen Saviour, our connection has been dissolved. and let us put on the armour of light-- described at length in Ep 6:11-18 .

entries.content_plain: 13. Let us walk honestly-- "becomingly," "seemingly" as in the day-- "Men choose the night for their revels, but our night is past, for we are all the children of the light and of the day ( 1Th 5:5 ): let us therefore only do what is fit to be exposed to the light of such a day." not in rioting and drunkenness-- varied forms of intemperance; denoting revels in general, usually ending in intoxication. not in chambering and wantonness-- varied forms of impurity; the one pointing to definite acts, the other more general. not in strife and envying-- varied forms of that venomous feeling between man and man which reverses the law of love.
entries.reader_content_plain: 13. Let us walk honestly-- "becomingly," "seemingly" as in the day-- "Men choose the night for their revels, but our night is past, for we are all the children of the light and of the day ( 1Th 5:5 ): let us therefore only do what is fit to be exposed to the light of such a day." not in rioting and drunkenness-- varied forms of intemperance; denoting revels in general, usually ending in intoxication. not in chambering and wantonness-- varied forms of impurity; the one pointing to definite acts, the other more general. not in strife and envying-- varied forms of that venomous feeling between man and man which reverses the law of love.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16655"/><div sID="gen32637" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16655"/><hi type="bold">14. But--</hi>to sum up all in one word.<div eID="gen32637" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32638" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ--</hi>in such wise that Christ only may be seen in you (see <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.3">2Co 3:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.3.27">Ga 3:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.4.24">Ep 4:24</reference>).<div eID="gen32638" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32639" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and make no provision--</hi>"take no forethought."<div eID="gen32639" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32640" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for the flesh, to fulfil the lust thereof--</hi>"Direct none of your attention to the cravings of your corrupt nature, how you may provide for their gratification."<div eID="gen32640" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32641" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Note, (1) How gloriously adapted is Christianity for human society in all conditions! As it makes war directly against no specific forms of government, so it directly recommends none. While its holy and benign principles secure the ultimate abolition of all iniquitous government, the reverence which it teaches for magistracy, under whatever form, as a divine institution, secures the loyalty and peaceableness of its disciples, amid all the turbulence and distractions of civil society, and makes it the highest interest of all states to welcome it within their pale, as in this as well as every other sense--</hi>"the salt of the earth, the light of the world" (<reference osisRef="Rom.13.1-Rom.5.2">Ro 13:1-5). (2</reference>) Christianity is the grand specific for the purification and elevation of all the social relations; inspiring a readiness to discharge all obligations, and most of all, implanting in its disciples that love which secures all men against injury from them, inasmuch as it is the fulfilling of the law (<reference osisRef="Rom.13.6-Rom.10.3">Ro 13:6-10). (3</reference>) The rapid march of the kingdom of God, the advanced stage of it at which we have arrived, and the ever-nearing approach of the perfect day--nearer to every believer the longer he lives--should quicken all the children of light to redeem the time, and, seeing that they look for such things, to be diligent, that they may be found of Him in peace, without spot and blameless (<reference osisRef="2Pet.3.14">2Pe 3:14</reference>). (<reference osisRef="2Pet.3.4">4</reference>) In virtue of "the expulsive power of a new and more powerful affection," the great secret of persevering holiness in all manner of conversation will be found to be "Christ IN US, the hope of glory" (<reference osisRef="Col.1.27">Col 1:27</reference>), and Christ ON US, as the character in which alone we shall be able to shine before men (<reference osisRef="2Cor.3.8">2Co 3:8</reference>) (<reference osisRef="Rom.13.14">Ro 13:14</reference>). <chapter eID="Rom.13"/>
entries.content_plain: 14. But-- to sum up all in one word. put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ-- in such wise that Christ only may be seen in you (see 2Co 3:3 ; Ga 3:27 ; Ep 4:24 ). and make no provision-- "take no forethought." for the flesh, to fulfil the lust thereof-- "Direct none of your attention to the cravings of your corrupt nature, how you may provide for their gratification." While its holy and benign principles secure the ultimate abolition of all iniquitous government, the reverence which it teaches for magistracy, under whatever form, as a divine institution, secures the loyalty and peaceableness of its disciples, amid all the turbulence and distractions of civil society, and makes it the highest interest of all states to welcome it within their pale, as in this as well as every other sense-- "the salt of the earth, the light of the world" ( Ro 13:1-5). (2 ) Christianity is the grand specific for the purification and elevation of all the social relations; inspiring a readiness to discharge all obligations, and most of all, implanting in its disciples that love which secures all men against injury from them, inasmuch as it is the fulfilling of the law ( Ro 13:6-10). (3 ) The rapid march of the kingdom of God, the advanced stage of it at which we have arrived, and the ever-nearing approach of the perfect day--nearer to every believer the longer he lives--should quicken all the children of light to redeem the time, and, seeing that they look for such things, to be diligent, that they may be found of Him in peace, without spot and blameless ( 2Pe 3:14 ). (2 ) Christianity is the grand specific for the purification and elevation of all the social relations; inspiring a readiness to discharge all obligations, and most of all, implanting in its disciples that love which secures all men against injury from them, inasmuch as it is the fulfilling of the law ( Ro 13:6-10).
